reviews.title: Payment Charged, but Paid Subscription not honored. Could you return my number and apologize?
reviews.text:
I’m extremely disappointed with Dingtone's handling of its paid subscription service.
I subscribed to Dingtone's Virtual Phone Number service on July 23, paying $4.99 plus applicable tax per month. My subscription was successfully renewed, and payments were automatically deducted from my Apple Account balance on July 23, August 23, September 23, and October 23.
However, despite the successful payment on October 23, 2026, Dingtone failed to renew my subscription or extend my virtual phone number's validity. Instead, my account displays a warning stating that my phone number will expire on November 3, 2026, as though the October payment had never been received.
The payment was successfully processed by Apple, and I have documentary evidence of the transaction.
How can a company collect payment for a subscription while failing to provide the corresponding paid service?
I expect Dingtone to investigate this billing discrepancy immediately and either restore my paid subscription and extend my phone number's validity accordingly or issue a full refund to my original Apple Account payment balance.
Customers should not have to pay for services they do not receive. I hope the developer takes this matter seriously and provides a prompt resolution.

reviews.title: Bad Quality and More expensive than original Careers.
reviews.text:
Here’s a honest review from a platinum level Dingtone user since 2017. I use the numbers for registrations and verifications to avoid spam calls and the services to communicate with acquaintances. 

The price increase of phone numbers from $4.99 to $23.99 and text charges from 0.5 credits to 3.5 Credits. 
The call quality became really bad these days, i barely hear anything even on speaker. Weak signals, poor reception and a hopeless customer care.

Awareness!! 
Do not believe the “0.5 credits per text” rule, that is completely false. it is actually 3.5 credits per text and some regions are 6 credits per text. 

Take note!! 
1 text = 145 characters 
So sending a paragraph or a long text message could cost you 20 credits or more.

Caution!! 
There’s a built in glitch that sends your messages twice or multiple times, if you mistakenly hit the send ➡️ button twice or multiple times. The action is usually delayed, So it’s technically designed to drain your credits. 

Warning!!! 
Do not buy phone numbers with Apple subscription because they charge the equivalent amount in credit yearly and you end up paying twice.

reviews.title: Terrible app
reviews.text:
I am writing this review to warn others about a severe issue with fraudulent charges. This app charged my iTunes account for a phone number that was never delivered. The transaction showed an "error," yet the full amount was immediately deducted from my payment method.

Furthermore, any credit you purchase within the app seems to be at high risk. I experienced my credit balance being drained overnight without any usage on my part. The service is unreliable, but their billing system is far too effective at taking money.

This is a serious pattern of behavior that warrants investigation by the Apple team. I feel completely scammed and would never recommend this app to anyone.
